description: I am a mechanical engineering student and full-stack dev building a "Lunar Landing Site Navigator." The app integrates the JPL Horizons API and NASA GeoTIFFs with a Next.js backend for server-side raycasting and a CesiumJS frontend. Join to help build a physics-accurate lunar exploration tool! I am looking for teammates skilled in 3D data visualization (Cesium/WebGL), UI/UX design, or astrophysics to help refine the terrain analysis and user experience.
summary:
MoonX (Lunar Landing Site Navigator) is a mission planning tool designed to help astronauts identify safe landing spots at the Moon's South Pole for future Artemis missions. 
Landing at the lunar South Pole comes with challenges like rough terrain and deep crater shadows, which can affect solar power and communication with Earth.
MoonX addresses this by combining NASA LOLA elevation data with live NASA JPL Horizons data to map out the lunar surface and track the positions of the Sun and Earth in real time.
It provides a 360-degree view of the surrounding mountain horizons and allows mission planners to scrub through a 48-hour timeline to identify the safest landing windows based on sunlight availability and direct communication with Earth.
details:
1. What MoonX Does & How It Works

MoonX is a lunar landing site navigator and line-of-sight analyzer built for lunar South Pole mission planning.

When a user selects a candidate landing site (such as Shackleton Crater Rim, Connecting Ridge, or Malapert Mountain):

  1. Ray-Tracing Real NASA Topography: The server accesses the NASA PDS LOLA 240-meter Digital Elevation Model (DEM) to ray-trace a physical, 360-degree panoramic mountain skyline for that exact coordinate in the Lunar Mean Earth (MOON_ME) reference frame.
  2. Celestial Ephemeris Integration: MoonX queries NASA JPL and NAIF SPICE APIs across a 48-hour mission window in 30-minute steps, calculating topocentric azimuth, elevation, distance, and apparent angular diameter for both the Sun and Earth.
  3. Line-of-Sight Determination: By comparing celestial trajectories against the local mountain ridges, MoonX computes exact clearance margins, classifying visibility into CLEAR LOS, GRAZING, or BLOCKED.
  4. Physical Space Viewport: In the 3D space viewport, the Sun remains stationary at high noon while the Moon physically rotates on its axis at ∼0.508∘/hour\sim 0.508^\circ/\text{hour}∼0.508∘/hour, showing true relative illumination across time.

2. Key Decisions & Creative UX Innovations

Throughout development, our team prioritized clarity over data clutter so that complex orbital mechanics can be understood instantly by flight controllers and the public alike:

  • Streamlined Mission Debrief: Instead of overwhelming the user with dense data tables and stacked timelines, we condensed the 48-hour timeline into an intuitive Mission Debrief highlighting three critical operational metrics:
    • Optimal Landing Window: Highlights the exact UTC window when both continuous solar power and direct radio to Earth are unblocked.
    • Battery Shadow Threshold: Flags the longest continuous eclipse period so engineers can verify battery depth-of-discharge.
    • Artemis Feasibility Score: A composite health indicator grading the site's overall landing safety.
  • 360° Mountain Skyline with 48h Solar Path Arc: Inside the horizon modal, planners can inspect the panoramic crater skyline with the Sun's full 48-hour sinusoidal arc overlaid, making it immediately visible when and where the Sun dips behind mountain peaks.
  • Strict Aerospace Transparency: Mission planners must never be misled by simulated data. If government servers encounter firewall timeouts, MoonX activates a topocentric analytical fallback, but prominently flags the telemetry with ▲ SIMULATED FALLBACK and scientific disclaimers on coordinate frame matching (LOLA ME datum vs. SPICE geodetics). When live feeds connect, it badges the data with ● LIVE NASA SPICE.

3. Benefits & Intended Impact

  • De-risking Artemis Surface Missions: Helps mission architects evaluate sites where elongated polar shadows threaten to freeze solar arrays or sever communication links with mission control.
  • Rapid Multi-Site Comparison: Allows planners to add up to 3 candidate landing scenarios simultaneously to compare illumination and link windows side-by-side.
  • Public & Educational Engagement: Provides a clean, dark-mode NASA mission HUD that makes lunar south-pole topography and orbital mechanics accessible to students, researchers, and space enthusiasts.

4. Tools, Coding Languages & Architecture

  • Framework & Language: Next.js (App Router), React 19, TypeScript.
  • Styling & HUD UI: Tailwind CSS, custom aerospace HUD design tokens.
    • NASA Planetary Data System (PDS) Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) LOLA LDEM_75S_240M topographic grid (V2.1).
    • NASA JPL Horizons Ephemeris API.
  • Deployment & Architecture: Cloud serverless deployment on Vercel with streaming cold-start handling, /tmp cache routing, and automated multi-endpoint HTTPS failover.
